paragraphs: Here's what I want you to take from this one, friend. God cares about the heart, not just the show. These elders sat down in front of Ezekiel looking religious, but the LORD says they had "set up idols in their hearts" (Ezekiel 14:3). You can sit in the front row, hold the right book and ask the right questions, and God still sees what you are holding on to inside.

Now look at what God does about it. He doesn't just scold. He says He wants to "take hold of the hearts of the people of Israel" (Ezekiel 14:5), and then He gives the way back: "Repent and turn away from your idols" (Ezekiel 14:6). That is a loving call, and the door is wide open for anyone, even the foreigner living among them (Ezekiel 14:7). I'll be honest, some of this passage is heavy, and I think it is heavy because God takes the distance between Him and His people seriously.

So here's the question for you, baker. What is sitting in your heart that is taking up the room God should have? You don't have to carry it around and keep tripping over it. God's goal is right there in the last verse: "Then they will be My people and I will be their God" (Ezekiel 14:11). He wants you close, and that is exactly the kind of guest list I'm baking for.
